# What the onion roots did

<!-- STEP id="results" -->
## The results

These root lengths, in centimetres, are read from the book's graph of this experiment.

| Day | Jar A (cm) | Jar B (cm) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.2 | 0.2 |
| 2 | 0.8 | 0.7 |
| 3 | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| 4 | 2.9 | 2.6 |
| 5 | 3.8 | 1.6 |
| 6 | 4.9 | 1.6 |
| 7 | 5.8 | 1.6 |

The book's graph shows the cut in Jar B after the day 4 reading, a day later than in the activity, so here Jar B drops from 2.6 cm to 1.6 cm on day 5. Either way, the result is the same: after the cut, the roots stop growing.

<!-- STEP id="trend" -->
## Jar A grows, Jar B stops

After the first day, the roots in Jar A grow by about 1 cm every day. The roots in Jar B become 1 cm shorter when their tips are cut, and after that their length does not change at all.

<!-- STEP id="answer" -->
## The answer

**So the answer to the prediction is that Jar B's roots stop getting longer, even though most of each root is still there.**
